title: Almost Golomb Sequences
summary: Golomb's sequence $(G(n))$ is the unique nondecreasing sequence of positive integers in which each $n$ appears exactly $G(n)$ times. It satisfies the global self-referential rule $G(G(n)+G(n-1)+\cdots+G(1))=n$, grows smoothly like a power of $n$ governed by the golden ratio, and is not $k$-regular for any $k\ge 2$. We introduce almost Golomb sequences, obtained by truncating the cumulative sum to a fixed size sliding window $r$: $a(a(n)+a(n-1)+\cdots+a(n-r+1))=n$.
